newsitem.title: USA: Ore. enters lawsuit against federal dam operators.
newsitem.headline: Ore. enters lawsuit against federal dam operators.

text.p: The state of Oregon filed last month to join a lawsuit brought by enviromentalists and fish conservationists against operators of federal hydroelectric dams in the Pacific Northwest.
A spokesman for the National Marine Fisheries Service (NMFS) in Portland, Ore., said Friday oral arguments in the U.S. District Court case are scheduled to start in March.

The environmentalists charge that NMFS, along with the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Bureau of Reclamation and Bonneville Power Administration, have not complied with a section of the Endangered Species Act.
The allegations include lack of proof that guidelines for dam operations will not jeoparize endangered salmon and that NMFS relied on unsupported analysis for its plans, Jones said.
The plaintiffs are asking the court to require the federal agencies to operate dams on the Columbia and Snake Rivers in a way that complies with the law.
Technical information is now being submitted to the court, with a judge expected to rule on the suit after oral arguments are presented, he added.
